title: Linked Lists

views.title: Linked Lists
views.intro: Use a dummy head whenever the head can change. Slow/fast pointers find the middle and the cycle; reversing the second half turns many problems (palindrome, reorder) into a merge of two lists. Draw the pointers before coding.
table: Middle, cycle entry, nth from end
Two lists, K lists by divide and conquer, sort list
Reorder, partition, rotate, copy with random pointer

files.desc: Reverse (range, k-group), swap pairs, middle, cycle, remove nth, merge, merge K, sort, reorder, palindrome, add numbers, intersection, dedupe II, partition, rotate, odd-even, copy random

pitfalls: Dummy head removes every "is it the head?" special case.
Save `next` BEFORE overwriting it when reversing.
Cycle entry: after slow meets fast, restart one pointer at the head and move both one step.

decisions.q: Reverse all, a segment, or in groups?
decisions.a: Iterative pointer flip; pull-to-front for ranges
Slow / fast, or a gap of n

decisions.q: Cycle present, and where does it start?

decisions.a: Dummy head merge; divide and conquer for K

decisions.q: Sort a list in O(n log n), O(1) extra?
Palindrome or reorder using the second half?
Clone with arbitrary pointers in O(1) space?

calibration: SDE2 bar: reverse list, merge two lists, detect cycle, remove nth from end, middle of list, add two numbers.
SDE3 bar: reverse k-group, merge K lists, sort list, reorder list, copy list with random pointer, LRU cache from scratch.
Staff bar (for context): in-place operations with proof of pointer invariants, lock-free list intuition, and skip-list / unrolled list tradeoffs.
